item.content:encoded:
UC Taps Public Markets Again for Funds

Urban Company is hungry for more cash. Despite sitting on over hundreds of crores in cash, the consumer services giant’s board will convene next week to consider a fresh fundraise. So, why is Urban Company heading back to the public markets less than a year after its IPO?

UC Seeks Fresh Capital: The startup’s board will meet on October 16 to consider raising capital through equity shares or convertible securities. Besides this, the board will also take a call on which route to take for the fundraise. But what makes this episode interesting is that UC was sitting on ₹2,019 Cr in cash and treasury investments at the end of June. Even ₹310.8 Cr of the startup’s ₹472 Cr fresh issue also remains unutilised. So, why is it chasing more money?

The Cash Guzzler: The likely pressure point is InstaHelp, UC’s instant services vertical. The company is investing heavily in the new arm to create a new category as competition continues to intensify from Snabbit and Pronto. On top of this, InstaHelp continues to weigh heavily on UC’s overall profitability, reporting an adjusted EBITDA loss of ₹132 Cr in Q1 FY27. 

Management expects InstaHelp to remain loss-making for the next few years and is unlikely to achieve breakeven before FY31

A Wider Trend: Urban Company’s post-IPO fundraise move reflects a broader pattern among listed new-age tech companies. For companies still investing in expansion, secondary issuances offer capital without interest obligations or repayment pressure. Strong share prices can also allow businesses to raise more money with less dilution. Rather than viewing an IPO as a final exit, founders are using public markets as an ongoing liquidity engine.

But, investors are also shifting focus from gross revenue to earnings per share and ROIC to ensure fresh money creates genuine accretion rather than capital hoarding. Amid this backdrop, will Urban Company’s latest fundraise find any takers? Let’s find out…

From The Editor’s Desk

DailyObjects’ Slow-Burn Playbook

  • From selling smartphone cases in 2014 to selling accessories and bags, DailyObjects has come a long way in the past decade. What has helped the brand move beyond a market dominated by low-cost, unbranded accessories is its design-led differentiation.
  • The startup reported a revenue of ₹200 Cr in FY26, and is targeting a ₹400 Cr top line and EBITDA profitability in FY27. This has come on the back of a richer product mix, greater offline contribution and supply-chain efficiencies.
  • DailyObjects also currently operates 13 exclusive brand outlets and is present in 300 Apple premium reseller stores. It plans to open two to three stores a month, add 30–35 stores in FY27 and build a network of 150–160 stores over five years.

GreenCell Bags ₹330 Cr

  • The EV startup has raised $34.6 Mn in an equity funding round led by Impact Fund Denmark to support the rollout of about 4,500 electric buses, execute its order book and streamline service delivery.
  • Founded in 2019, GreenCell Mobility acquires e-buses from contract manufacturers and then deploys them for both intercity and intracity travel. It claims to operate more than 1,200 electric buses and runs over 270 charging stations. It has raised $37 Mn to date.
  • The fundraise comes as the homegrown electric bus ecosystem continues to scale rapidly on the back of growing government procurement, GCC models, rising EV adoption and electric transition mandates.

UPI MDR Saga Continues

  • The National Payments Corporation of India has deferred the re-introduction of merchant discount rate on select UPI transactions. Instead of the earlier October 15 rollout, the MDR will now be implemented “immediately after Diwali”.
  • The NPCI said it took the decision keeping the festive season in mind. The revised implementation date will be notified separately. This follows reports that the Centre was considering delaying the MDR rollout to January 2027.
  • Under the proposed framework, merchants would be charged an MDR of 0.40% on P2M UPI transactions above ₹2,000, capped at ₹300 per transaction. The move had invited significant push back from retailers, which had demanded the rollback of MDR.

DealShare CEO Exits

  • Kamaldeep Singh has stepped down as the CEO of the troubled ecommerce unicorn after a three year-long stint. He has now joined electric mobility solutions provider Indofast Energy as its new CEO. DealShare has not announced Singh’s replacement.
  • The exit comes amid a slew of departures at the beleaguered ecommerce unicorn. CFO Ashish Shah is also looking to exit the startup, while DealShare’s founding team – Sourjyendu Medda, Vineet Rao, Sankar Bora and Rajat Shikhar – all exited in 2024.
  • Known for online grocery delivery in tier-II+ cities, DealShare is trying to douse fires on multiple fronts. The startup has been scaling down its operations as online business has dwindled to “next to zero”. It is also in talks with Truemeds for a potential fire sale.

Freshworks To Acquire Torii

  • The Nasdaq-listed SaaS major has signed a definitive agreement to acquire the SaaS management platform for an undisclosed amount. Freshworks expects the deal to close by 2026-end.
  •  By integrating Torii’s SaaS management capabilities into Freshservice, the listed giant aims to help its clients have a better visibility of their AI usage and spending. 
  • Founded in 2010, Freshworks offers SaaS tools to help enterprises manage customer engagement, sales, IT service management, marketing and automation. It reported a net profit of $3.2 Mn in the quarter ended June 2026 against a revenue of $237.4 Mn.

Inc42 Markets

Inc42 Startup Spotlight

How Lickicious Is Betting Big On India’s Pet Parents

India’s pet parents want more than generic kibble or home-cooked meals. Yet, specialised and nutrition-led options remain limited. To solve this, Lickicious is building a pet nutrition brand around food, treats and supplements for dogs and cats.

A Desi Pet Brand: Founded in 2024, Lickicious sells dry and wet foods, treats, supplements and nutritional toppers for dogs and cats. It positions its products around palatability and balanced nutrition, while the startup also operates its own manufacturing setup.

Owning The Supply Chain: Unlike brands that rely entirely on contract manufacturing, Lickicious runs its own manufacturing setup and is developing a 60,000 sq ft manufacturing and distribution footprint. The startup claims that this will increase production capacity, improve supply reliability and strengthen quality control.

The Road Ahead: Backed by Prath Ventures, the startup now plans to scale its R&D and expand into new categories, formats, species and sales channels. The brand is targeting ₹100 Cr in annual revenue going forward and aims to become one of the biggest pet food companies in the country over the next decade.

With India’s pet food market projected to become a $2.2 Bn opportunity by 2030, can Lickicious scale into a durable pet food brand for dogs and cats?

Infographic Of The Day

From Indian textiles and traditional motifs to handcrafted accessories and heritage wear, homegrown craftsmanship is finding a growing audience beyond borders. Can Bharat’s next global D2C success story be woven from its own traditions?

item.title: [Update] Blume, Speciale Invest & 11 Other AIFs Selected For Deploying ₹7,131 Cr Under RDI Fund
item.dc:creator: Anne Florentyna
item.description: Original | Oct 14, 02:37 IST The government has selected Blume Ventures, Speciale Invest, Chiratae Ventures and 16 others as…
item.content:encoded:
Original | Oct 14, 02:37 IST

The government has selected Blume Ventures, Speciale Invest, Chiratae Ventures and 16 others as second-level fund managers (SLFM) for deploying ₹7,131 Cr from the ₹1 Lakh Cr research, development and innovation (RDI) fund.

This is the first cohort of the SLFM under the fund. Overall, the empowered group of secretaries (EGoS) under the science ministry has approved 14 alternative investment funds (AIFs) and five focused research organisations (FROs) for this purpose earlier this month.

The other selected AIFs also include YourNest Capital Advisors, Sixth Sense Ventures, Celesta India, AdvantEdge Investment Managers, IvyCap Ventures, Ideaspring Capital Fund, TVS Capital Funds, AMA Capital Advisors, Translation Endeavors and “Campus”.

Meanwhile, the selected FROs include the likes of IISc Bengaluru’s AI & Robotics Technology Park (ARTPARK), Centre for Cellular and Molecular Platforms (CCAMP) in Bengaluru, IIT-Madras Research Park, Pilani Innovation & Entrepreneurship Development Society (PIEDS) at BITS-Pilani, and Society for Innovation & Entrepreneurship (SINE) at IIT-Bombay.

Update | Oct 12, 21:48 IST

Central government-backed ₹1 Lakh Cr Research, Development and Innovation (RDI) Fund has approved 19 second-level fund managers (SLFMs) with a total commitment of ₹7,131 Cr.

The Ministry of Science and Technology’s Empowered Group of Secretaries (EGoS) approved 14 alternative investment funds (AIFs) and five focused research organisations (FROs) for this purpose earlier this month, the ministry announced. 

The selected entities will channel capital from the RDI Fund to eligible technology enterprises undertaking research, development and innovation activities at Technology Readiness Level (TRL) 4 and above.

The fund managers are also expected to mobilise private capital equivalent to the RDI Fund’s contribution, potentially expanding the pool of financing available to research-driven businesses.

Alongside approving the first cohort of fund managers, the EGoS approved five additional technologies for coverage under the RDI Fund. The government did not specify these technologies in its announcement.

The government said it would continue inviting applications and onboarding additional cohorts of fund managers, expanding the reach of the scheme and encouraging public-private investment in India’s research and innovation ecosystem.

Launched in November 2025, the RDI Scheme has an overall outlay of ₹1 Lakh Cr and aims to address the funding gap faced by companies developing high-risk, high-impact technologies. It is managed by an independent business unit housed within the Anusandhan National Research Foundation (ANRF), under the Department of Science and Technology (DST).

The fund is designed to spur private investment in research-intensive businesses. However, its impact on investor sentiment, however, remains unclear. In August, The Indian Express reported that nearly two-thirds of the more than ₹2,000 Cr allocated to deeptech companies under the scheme had gone to firms linked to members of the panel involved in selecting beneficiaries. The report raised concerns about potential conflicts of interest.

Inc42’s Q3 2026 Indian Investor Ranking & Sentiment Survey, which covered 85 institutional investors, found that 52% considered disclosure and recusal safeguards adequate, but said visibility into the process remained limited.

Another 25% viewed the issue as a governance failure that required independent oversight, while 14% said potential conflicts could be managed through disclosure and recusal. The remaining 9% said the issue was not a concern, arguing that the focus should be on selecting the right companies.

As per Inc42’s ‘Indian Tech Startup Funding Report, Q3 2026’, deeptech startup funding in the September quarter zoomed 176% YoY to $290 Mn raised across 28 deals, compared with $105 Mn across 29 deals in Q3 2025. The sector outpaced the broader startup ecosystem, where funding grew 5% to $2.2 Bn.

item.title: Freshworks To Acquire Torii To Expand AI Spend Governance Offerings
item.dc:creator: Gaurav Bagur
item.description: Nasdaq-listed SaaS major Freshworks has signed a definitive agreement to acquire Torii, a SaaS management platform, to extend its IT…
item.content:encoded:
Nasdaq-listed SaaS major Freshworks has signed a definitive agreement to acquire Torii, a SaaS management platform, to extend its IT service management tool, Freshservice, into AI and software spend governance. The transaction is expected to close in the quarter ending December 2026. 

Founded in 2017 by Uri Haramati, Uri Nativ and Tal Bereznitskey in New York, Torii helps enterprises track AI consumption at the token level, attribute usage to specific internal teams, forecast spend trajectories, and set operational budget limits. 

By integrating its SaaS management capabilities into Freshservice, Freshworks aims to enable organisations to have better visibility of their AI usage. The system provides IT and finance departments with continuous oversight, replacing manual spreadsheet reconciliation with real-time analytics.

“Modern IT teams are being asked to govern more of the business than ever, with less visibility into what it costs. Freshservice already gives IT one place to see everything they run. With Torii, that same view now extends to software and AI spend — what’s running, who’s using it, and what it costs, so finance and IT stop reconciling spreadsheets and start making decisions together,” said Freshworks CEO and President Dennis Woodside. 

Founded in 2010 by Girish Mathrubootham and Shanmugam Krishnasamy, Freshworks offers a suite of cloud-based software to help companies manage customer engagement, sales, IT service management and marketing.

After Mathrubootham exited the company in 2024, it has sought to reinvent itself as an AI-native enterprise platform under Woodside’s leadership. Apart from introducing AI-led offerings like vertical AI agents and workflow automation tools, it also underwent a major restructuring earlier this year, trimming 11% of its workforce or around 500 employees, citing automation of work. 

Growing adoption of its AI products helped Freshworks get back into the black in the quarter ended June 2026. The company reported a net profit of $3.2 Mn as against a net loss of $1.7 Mn in the year-ago period and a net loss of $4.8 Mn in the previous quarter. Meanwhile, its revenue grew 16% YoY to $237.4 Mn.

item.title: [Update] Adani Enterprises, Jabil Sign MoU To Set Up AI-Focused Joint Venture
item.dc:creator: Gaurav Bagur
item.description: Update | October 13, 20:00 IST Adani Group’s flagship business Adani Enterprises and US-based manufacturing company Jabil Inc have signed…
item.content:encoded:
Update | October 13, 20:00 IST

Adani Group’s flagship business Adani Enterprises and US-based manufacturing company Jabil Inc have signed a non-binding memorandum of understanding (MoU) to establish a 50:50 joint venture for manufacturing and assembling AI and data centre equipment in India.

The proposed partnership aims to produce AI racks, servers, storage, networking equipment, and power and cooling systems to cater to India’s rapidly growing data centre capacity. It targets the expanding domestic market as well as international exports.

“At Adani, our vision is to expand up the AI value chain evolving from powering and hosting AI infrastructure to engineering and manufacturing the critical systems that will define the next generation of computing. Our proposed joint venture with Jabil marks a strategic step towards this future, combining Jabil’s world-class engineering and manufacturing capabilities with Adani’s integrated strengths in energy, infrastructure and data centres to help build the physical backbone of the global AI economy,” said Adani Group chairman Gautam Adani.

With this MoU, the earlier agreement between Adani and Jabil has now taken a more concrete form, although its realisation remains subject to regulatory approvals and the execution of definitive agreements.

Original | June 15, 22:12 IST

Indian conglomerate Adani Group has partnered with US-based manufacturing company Jabil Inc to build vertically-integrated AI and data centre infrastructure in India. 

The two companies intend to set up multi-gigawatt manufacturing capacity in India for high-density AI racks. They will produce AI-ready hardware such as liquid-cooled AI racks, servers, storage units, and networking systems to serve the needs of global hyperscalers and enterprise data centers. 

Beyond computing hardware, the platform plans to manufacture supporting infrastructure components, including power distribution units, coolant distribution units, transformers, switchgears, and advanced thermal management systems.

The companies are currently finalising operational frameworks and formal documentation to execute the manufacturing roadmap, with no definitive timeline announced. 

The partnership with Jabil is in line with Adani Group’s bid to double down on AI. In February, Adani announced one of the world’s largest integrated energy-compute commitments with a direct investment of $100 Bn to develop renewable-energy-powered, hyperscale AI-ready data centres by 2035. 

Later, the Adani Group was said to be exploring partnerships with Meta, Google among others, to set up data centres in the country. 

To note, the conglomerate has also tied up with Uber to set up its first data centre in India, which would become operational later this year. 

The Adani-Jabil partnership comes at a time when the global market opportunity for AI compute infrastructure is projected to zoom past the $3 Tn mark over the next seven years. India’s data centre capacity is projected to reach 5-8 GW by 2030, driven by growing AI demand, cloud expansion, and data localisation requirements. 

Notably, India’s technology supply chains are increasingly shifting toward domestic manufacturing, given the focus on data sovereignty and the requirements of the DPDP Act. 

Along with the Adani Group, companies like Reliance Industries and Amazon are also betting on capturing this momentum.

For instance, Reliance announced a partnership with Meta last week that would see the oil-to-telecom conglomerate set up a 168 MW AI-enabled data centre in Gujarat’s Jamnagar, powered by sustainable energy, within two years. 

Amazon has committed an investment of $12.7 Bn towards cloud infrastructure in India by 2030, while OpenAI is planning to set up a 1 GW data centre in India in partnership with TCS.

item.title: GreenCell Mobility Raises ₹330 Cr To Expand Electric Bus Fleet
item.dc:creator: Anne Florentyna
item.description: Everstone Capital-backed EV startup GreenCell Mobility has raised ₹330 Cr ($34.6 Mn) in an equity funding round led by Impact…
item.content:encoded:
Everstone Capital-backed EV startup GreenCell Mobility has raised ₹330 Cr ($34.6 Mn) in an equity funding round led by Impact Fund Denmark to support the rollout of about 4,500 electric buses currently under deployment.

The Mumbai-based startup is eyeing expanding its fleet to more than 5,000 e-buses across 105 cities across India. 

“Our focus is on executing our order book with rigour, strengthening service delivery and ensuring that the organisation keeps pace with the size and complexity of our operations. This equity investment gives us greater headroom to accelerate our plans while maintaining the standards of reliability, efficiency and customer experience that are fundamental to our business,” GreenCell Mobility managing director and chief executive Devndra Chawla said.

Founded in 2019, GreenCell Mobility focuses on deploying and operating electric buses for public transportation. It acquires electric buses via contract manufacturing arrangements with vendors and then deploys them for both intercity and intracity travel.

Backed by Eversource Capital, a joint venture between Everstone Capital and Lightsource, GreenCell primarily operates under the brand NueGo. 

It claims to operate more than 1,200 electric buses in India, including 900 on intra-city routes, 300 under its NueGo brand for inter-city travel, and 50 for MSRTC. The startup also runs over 270 charging stations to support its fleet.

The startup previously raised $37 Mn from World Bank’s International Finance Corporation and also counts Eversource Capital, British International Investment and Tata Capital among its backers. 

India’s electric bus segment has so far drawn strong interest from development finance institutions and lenders backing vehicle deployments under long-term public transport contracts. GreenCell’s latest round suggested that investors are also beginning to back the operating platform layer in the category, not just asset financing.

The investment highlights the role of institutional capital in expanding electric public transportation infrastructure in India. Large-scale electric bus deployments require funding not only for vehicles but also for the operational capabilities and charging infrastructure needed to support them.

Earlier in March, electric bus manufacturer PMI Electro Mobility, along with its electric bus platform Allfleet, has signed a definitive agreement with private equity giant KKR for an investment commitment of up to $310 Mn, to help scale the electric bus platform and focus on expanding its presence across India. PMI subsequently filed for an IPO via the confidential route last month.
